title: The Lantern Street Night Market
script:
narrator: The Lantern Street Night Market.
<#0.6#>
<parallel room="outdoors" stage="Ada=-0.6, Wren=0.15, Tomas=0.6, Vendor=0.85, Stranger=-0.75">
  <sound loop="true" volume="0.3" duration="30" name="market_crowd">Busy outdoor night market crowd, chatter, laughter, sizzling food stalls, distant clatter</sound>
  <sound loop="true" volume="0.35" duration="40" name="busker_guitar">Bright jangling acoustic guitar busker tune, strummed steel strings, upbeat folk, no vocals</sound>
  <sequential>
    narrator: Under the paper lanterns, [warm, amused] three friends stood arguing about who had lost the van keys.
    Ada: You had them last, [accusing] I watched you lock the —
    Tomas: I did not lock anything, [defensive, fast] you drove, so you —
    Ada: I drove there, [exasperated] you drove the —
    Wren: Stop, both of you! [laughing, firm] Turn out your pockets, right now.
    <parallel>
      <sound name="pocket_items" duration="3" pan="0.6">Coins and a crumpled paper wrapper dropped onto a wooden crate</sound>
      narrator: Tomas emptied his jacket onto a crate: [dry] a bus ticket, two coins, a dumpling wrapper.
    </parallel>
    Tomas: See, nothing, [smug] so it has to be —
    Ada: Don't you dare say it's me, [snapping] last time they were in your —
    Tomas: In my shoe, once, [sheepish] that was <emphasis>once</emphasis>.
    Vendor: <far> Last call for noodles, [shouting, cheerful] last call!
    <parallel>
      <sound name="passing_truck" duration="6" pan="-0.95,0.95">Delivery truck rumbling slowly past, low diesel engine growl and a loose tailgate rattling, passing by close</sound>
      narrator: A delivery truck rumbled slowly past [steady] from one end of the street to the other.
    </parallel>
    Wren: Wait, [hushed, alert] listen.
    Stranger: <far> Did someone lose a set of keys? [calling out] Blue keychain, anyone?
    Tomas: Blue keychain, [whispering] that's —
    Ada: That's ours! [already running, calling] Hey, over here, those are —
    Tomas: Mine, [grinning, giving in] I'm the one who lost them, fine, I admit it.
  </sequential>
</parallel>
<#1.0#>
<parallel room="large_hall" stage="Ada=-0.5, Wren=0.15, Tomas=0.5">
  <sound loop="true" volume="0.25" duration="40" name="church_organ">Soft sustained church pipe organ chord drone, gentle and calm, no vocals</sound>
  <sequential>
    <parallel>
      <sound name="church_door" duration="4" pan="-0.4">Heavy wooden church door closing with a deep echo in a stone hall</sound>
      narrator: They ducked into the old stone church, [quiet, reverent] where every footstep echoed off the high walls.
    </parallel>
    Wren: Okay, [quietly] nobody touches the keys again except —
    Ada: Except me.
    Tomas: Except you, [agreeing, then sly] although technically, if you think about who parked —
    Ada: Tomas.
    Tomas: Right, sorry, [meek] keys stay with Ada.
  </sequential>
</parallel>
<#0.6#>
narrator: Outside, [fading, warm] the busker started a brand new song.

speakers.name: narrator
speakers.description: A female voice: mid forties, warm alto with an easy smile in it, clear articulation, relaxed storytelling pace. Clean dry studio recording.
speakers.preview_text: The night market on Lantern Street was loud with music, and the smell of fried dumplings drifted between the stalls while the lanterns swayed overhead.

speakers.name: Ada
speakers.description: A female voice: late twenties, bright quick mezzo-soprano, sharp and confident, fast conversational pacing with crisp consonants. Clean dry studio recording.
speakers.preview_text: I am telling you, I watched you put them in your pocket, and now you are standing there acting like you have never seen a set of keys in your life.

speakers.name: Tomas
speakers.description: A male voice: around thirty, easygoing light baritone, playful and a little defensive, quick rhythm with clear diction. Clean dry studio recording.
speakers.preview_text: Look, I checked every pocket twice, my jacket, my jeans, even the little coin pocket nobody ever uses, and there is nothing in there but a bus ticket.

speakers.name: Wren
speakers.description: A female voice: early thirties, calm smooth soprano, amused and steady, measured pacing with soft warmth. Clean dry studio recording.
speakers.preview_text: Both of you, take a breath, empty your pockets onto the crate, and we will sort this out before the noodle stall closes for the night.

speakers.name: Vendor
speakers.description: A male voice: fifties, loud cheerful street-vendor tenor, booming projection and a hearty sing-song call. Clean dry studio recording.
speakers.preview_text: Fresh hand-pulled noodles, hot broth, extra chili, come and get them now before the pot runs dry for tonight, last bowls of the evening.

speakers.name: Stranger
speakers.description: A male voice: forties, friendly helpful baritone, raised calling voice, unhurried and kind. Clean dry studio recording.
speakers.preview_text: Excuse me, I found these lying by the dumpling stall a minute ago, so if anyone around here is missing them, just come over and grab them.
